# Why is net_forces_w in Isaac Lab humanoid footbot only containing normal force, and where to get the tangential friction force?

> **Current answer:** Maintainer explicitly states that net_forces_w is the net normal contact force in the world frame, and does not include the complete friction component. The old version of the underlying get_friction_data(dt) function requires manual aggregation, and the original author reported full zero results after testing. The official merge of PR #3563 has enabled track_friction_forces and reading friction_forces_w; this field is aggregated by env/body/filter and has official testing. Use this field only after verifying the target version includes PR #3563 and is configured appropriately.

## Key terms

- Net normal contact force (净法向接触力)
- Friction force (摩擦力)
- Contact sensor (接触传感器)
- World frame (世界坐标系)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why is net_forces_w only containing normal force when there is clear friction? How to obtain the tangential friction force?
- Original graph shows z-component of contact foot about 667 N/543 N, while x is about 8e-05/6e-05 and y is zero.
- Another user's curve shows only one world axis component varying with dragging, and the other two curves remain at zero.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab ContactSensor, long slender cylindrical foot collision geometry; original post does not provide version; PR #3563 was merged into the official repository on 2025-12-10.

## Priority diagnostics

- First confirm the semantics of the field: net_forces_w is the net normal contact force in the world frame, not the sum of normal and friction forces.
- Confirm whether the target version includes PR #3563, whether track_friction_forces is enabled, the non-empty filter_prim_paths_expr, and valid max_contact_data_count_per_prim.

## Possible causes

- Reading the compatible net_forces_w field that only carries normal force, but expecting tangential friction force.

## Attempts

- The maintainer suggests directly calling contact_physx_view.get_friction_data(dt) and reminds that the format must be manually aggregated.
- The original author tried the old path and reported full zero, so this path did not form a verified fix in their environment.

## Effective fixes

- In versions containing PR #3563, enable ContactSensorCfg.track_friction_forces and read ContactSensorData.friction_forces_w; the official implementation aggregates friction data by env/body/filter and includes contact/none testing.

## Result

- PR #3563 merged, issue marked as completed; PR testing confirms friction_forces_w is consistent with the underlying get_friction_data aggregation result.

## Limitations

- Issue with get_friction_data(dt) in early versions was not successful in the original author's environment, so it cannot be treated as a universal fix.
- The two original graphs do not include Isaac Lab versions, friction coefficient, units, or complete experimental configuration, so the curve size cannot be used to infer real friction parameters.

## Safety notes

- Before using for real-world sliding/friction cone detection, validate coordinate system, sign, filtering, sampling period, and sensor/model errors; simulation contact forces are not substitutes for real-world sensor data.

## Image and visual evidence

- The verified curve from comment 2733805649 shows only the blue X curve varying between -3 and -10 with several peaks, while the orange Y and green Z curves remain at zero; coordinates are only Force/Time with no units, version, or friction parameters, so it only supports the 'other two axes are zero' symptom, not proving force calibration.
- The MuJoCo screenshot from comment 2752798128 shows multiple shallow blue upward arrows and numerical annotations near the robot's foot, but no legend, coordinate axes, or units; it only expresses the author's desire for a complete contact force visualization, not as a proof of Isaac Lab fix results.

## Applicability boundary

- Applies to Isaac Lab ContactSensor; explicit friction_forces_w path requires the target version to include PR #3563 and be configured to enable friction tracking.
